name: Zachary Taylor
role: Twelfth US president (1849–1850), career army general
summary: Zachary Taylor, a career soldier and slaveholding planter, won the presidency as a Whig war hero with no platform. He held that the executive should defer to Congress, favoured a protective tariff and a sound banking system, urged California and New Mexico to seek statehood to avoid sectional conflict, and said he would use force against secession.

sources.title: Inaugural Address (5 March 1849), Miller Center
sources.author: Zachary Taylor
sources.usedFor: Principles of his presidency: the Constitution, neutrality and no entangling alliances, appointments, debt, army and navy.

sources.title: First Annual Message (4 December 1849), Miller Center
sources.author: Zachary Taylor
sources.usedFor: Tariff, banking and the subtreasury, agricultural bureau, the Union, the slave trade, executive and legislative powers, the army.

sources.title: Message Regarding Newly Acquired Territories (23 January 1850), Miller Center
sources.author: Zachary Taylor
sources.usedFor: California and New Mexico statehood, self-government and domestic institutions of states, territories.

sources.title: Message Regarding Treaty with Great Britain (22 April 1850), Miller Center
sources.author: Zachary Taylor
sources.usedFor: The Clayton-Bulwer treaty: canal neutrality, no annexation of Central American republics.

sources.title: Letter to Captain J. S. Allison (22 April 1848), reprinted in The Weekly Raleigh Register, 16 August 1848 (DigitalNC OCR page)
sources.author: Zachary Taylor
sources.usedFor: His campaign statement: Whig but not an ultra Whig, independent of party, the veto only for clear unconstitutionality or manifest haste, the executive's wishes not to control Congress, the will of Congress on tariff, currency and improvements, war a calamity and no conquest.

sources.title: Zachary Taylor: Domestic Affairs, Miller Center essay
sources.author: Michael Holt
sources.usedFor: His stated views: he would hang anyone disrupting the Union by force, opposed Clay's compromise, presidency above party.

sources.title: Zachary Taylor: Campaigns and Elections, Miller Center essay
sources.author: Michael Holt
sources.usedFor: His stated views before 1849: sound banking and Jackson's destruction of the Second Bank, veto only for unconstitutional laws.

sources.title: Zachary Taylor: Life Before the Presidency, Miller Center essay
sources.author: Michael Holt
sources.usedFor: His stated views on citizen militia and on separating settlers from Native Americans.

notes: First audit. Taylor never voted before 1848, ran without a platform and served sixteen months, leaving four messages: the inaugural, the 1849 annual message, and two 1850 special messages, all read in full by theme (statehood, tariff, banking, Union, executive power, neutrality, army, the slave trade, the Isthmus canal), plus Holt's Miller Center essays on his life, campaign, domestic and foreign affairs. His record as a slave owner is cited as record; his Mexican War command and Indian wars are not answers because no statement is about them. His Mexican War letters (Letters of Zachary Taylor from the Battle-fields of the Mexican War, 1908, HathiTrust scan text) were searched for slavery, tariff, bank, annexation, militia and party: they are camp and command correspondence and settle none of the statements. The first Allison letter of 22 April 1848 is read from a newspaper reprint. Government and world statements beyond neutrality, the Union and the executive are thin because his presidency was short and his messages are brief.
